As companies are increasingly data-driven, there is demand for business professionals with knowledge, skills, and abilities in business analytics and artificial intelligence.
As a result, there are many job opportunities and high average starting salaries associated with positions at a wide range of organizations.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages)

2 The objective of the Quantum Computing Certificate program is to prepare those with a degree in a STEM discipline to pivot to a job/career in quantum computing. The demand for a quantum workforce has been emphasized in the National Quantum Initiative Act (https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/house- bill/6227). For many of those who might be interested, the option of pursuing an MS or PHD is not possible because of time or expense. This certificate will present the information base to allow a person working in industry or government to advance their careers in an exciting new direction. The four courses are designed to a) refresh a background in math, with an emphasis on the language of quantum mechanics, b) establish a foundation in quantum mechanics, c) apply the foundation to the design of quantum algorithms, and d) expand the knowledge of quantum computing to the technology involved in computation, teleportation, cryptography and circuitry. With this background, a person working with a degree in a STEM discipline will have the opportunity to expand their horizons and become productive in a new field. Our immediate outreach was to NUWC, and they circulated the program to the 8 other warfare centers. The response has been positive. We also contacted some companies to test the attractiveness of this type of certificate and have found similar interest. A8. Signature of the President Marc Parlange A9. RATIONALE: There should be a demonstrable need for the program.
B1.
Explain and quantify the needs addressed by this program, and present evidence that the program fulfills these needs.
While there are abundant interests and investments in Quantum Computing from the major technology companies (e.g.
Microsoft, Google, IBM…), there are few options for those who want to advance their knowledge.
URI is one of only a handful of universities in the country offering an MS in Quantum Computing.
Yet, for many, the time and expense to pursue a graduate degree is an insurmountable hurdle.
NSF recently had an RFP to encourage universities to begin graduate programs in order to increase the number of trained researchers and to close the perceived gap in personnel with other countries.
Quantum Computing has the potential to revolutionize the way computation is carried out and the economic benefits will be substantial.
Our proposed certificate program gives an additional option.
A student completing the certificate program will have both a foundational understanding as well as the practical knowledge to apply and design quantum algorithms.

In addition, with the embedded project that is threaded through the courses, the student will have a fundamental understanding of more general aspects of quantum sensing, teleportation, cryptography, circuitry and communication B2.
What is the economic need and workforce data related to the program?
The quantum revolution that is taking place will change the way computing is done.
Computations that would require hundreds or thousands of years will be accomplished in minutes on a quantum computer.
For example, the current cryptography protocols, rely on the impossibility of factoring large numbers in any reasonable time.
Quantum computers will be able to do the calculations in near real-time.
The quantum industry needs a workforce to address quantum sensors, quantum networking and communication, quantum hardware, quantum algorithms and the facilitation of technology.
There are 5 main types of technical careers in the quantum industry: engineer, technician, application researcher, experimental scientist, and theorist.
The certificate will support the first three of these job categories.

A certificate in Quantum Computing will open doors for a multitude of jobs and academic opportunities.

4 quantum computing)- Zurich Instruments, Quantum Computing Theorist- Raytheon, Quantum Computing Experimentalist – Raytheon, Research Scientist: Quantum Computation – IBM, Quantum Computing Researcher-IBM, Quantum Software Development – Microsoft, Senior Quantum Engineer- Rigetti Quantum Computing, Quantum Compiler Developer- Intel.
The number of such jobs posted is well over 100.
Having a certificate in Quantum Computing, will position our graduates for jobs, with anticipated starting salaries ranging from $80K -$120K (based on a review of job offerings in the industrial sector).
